items.title: First we shape AI, thereafter AI shapes us
items.summary:
When we put new technology into the world, we need human-centered methods to understand their impact. This talk will present three focus areas of my research in how people use AI and how that shapes them; 1. The cognitive and metacognitive costs of AI, 2. How people red-team LLMs in the wild, and 3. Hacc-Man - an arcade game for fostering AI literacy.

Bio: Nanna Inie, Assistant Professor, IT-University of Copenhagen

People describe Nanna as "a methodological savant", "a Pandora's Box of unfiltered opinions", and "who?" She uses mixed-methods to study how humans use technology to extend their cognition, evaluate how technology affects human cognition in return, and to transform findings into the design of novel technologies.

She is an assistant professor at the IT-University of Copenhagen and a lecturer at the University of Washington. Her specializations are cognitive augmentation tools, computing education, and AI safety in real-world settings.

items.title: Why the Best AI Stories Aren't About AI (with Steve Mock)
items.summary:
#AIForGood #AISavedMe #VibeCoding

In Episode #1009, Steve Mock (investor at Blumberg Capital, five-time entrepreneur, and creator of aisavedme.org), joins @JonKrohnLearns to explore the quiet layer of everyday AI adoption that rarely gets documented. After his 84-year-old father asked a deceptively simple question, “How does one use AI?”, Steve built a place for people to share how AI is actually helping them. The stories that came in surprised him: they’re rarely about the technology and almost always about human outcomes, caregiving, communication, learning, confidence and connection. 

This episode is brought to you by: 
• Anthropic: https://claude.ai/superdata
• Acceldata: https://www.acceldata.io
• Gurobi: https://www.superdatascience.com/gurobi
• Cisco: https://outshift.cisco.com/

Interested in sponsoring a SuperDataScience Podcast episode? Email natalie@superdatascience.com for sponsorship information.

In this episode you will learn:
• (00:00:00) Introduction
• (00:02:02) Where “AI Saved Me” came from, an 84-year-old dad’s simple question
• (00:14:27) The healthcare pattern, using AI to become your own advocate
• (00:23:36) The education pattern, personalized study and simulated office hours
• (00:28:32) The fulfillment pattern, offloading grunt work to focus on what matters
• (00:44:13) Building the whole site as a non-programmer
• (00:52:33) The investor’s lens, vertical AI and the “data flywheel” moat

items.title: Can a Standard Mac Really Run Sophisticated Models Without Lag?
items.summary:
Yes, your Mac can do more than you think.

In this short, Keiji Kamigusa answers one of the biggest questions about local AI: can a standard Mac really run sophisticated models without painful lag?

Thanks to Apple Silicon and modern local AI tools, running useful models on your own machine is becoming surprisingly practical. That means you can build private chatbots, RAG apps, voice tools, and other AI applications locally, without defaulting to expensive cloud APIs or a dedicated GPU rig.

Build Applications with Local AI Models on a Mac shows you how to get started with real projects that run on your Mac and help you understand what local AI can actually do.

If you’ve been assuming “my laptop isn’t enough,” this short may change your mind.

Learn more: https://hubs.la/Q04mY6wQ0

items.title: My Biggest Career Gamble Yet (Towards AI)
items.summary:
I have been hiding a major AI startup story for two years. Learn why I left my PhD to build the next chapter of my career.

This video details the trajectory of my AI career path and the specific problem that forced me to choose between academia and industry. If you are currently navigating your own tech career journey or trying to figure out how to transition from academic research into practical application, this breakdown provides the context you need.

I share the math, the models, and the specific motivations behind leaving a master's program to launch an AI company. By understanding the challenges I faced in 2020, you will (hopefully) gain clarity on how to align your own technical interests with long-term professional goals. We explore the reality of learning AI at a high level and what it takes to actually ship a product.

Subscribe for weekly AI breakdowns, and let me know in the comments if you are currently deciding between academia and industry.

items.title: Try This Awesome AI Video Transition!
items.summary:
How to "Time Travel" in your next video with this SUPER easy editing trick!

You don't need complex VFX software to create seamless, mind-bending transitions anymore. Here is a straightforward way to jump between locations using AI tools like Runway, Kling, or Leonardo:

Step 1: Record your intro in Location A, then head to Location B. Try to wear the same outfit and match your pose at the start of the second clip—it makes the final transition much more believable.
Step 2: Take a screenshot of the very last frame of Clip A, and the very first frame of Clip B.
Step 3: Upload these two images as your starting and ending keyframes in an AI tool (I used Runway's Seedance 2.0 for the edit you see in this video).
Step 4: Use a prompt like this: “The camera shoots up like a big jump transition and reveals the second location in one smooth motion. The man does not speak.” (Pro-tip: Adding "does not speak" stops the AI from generating weird facial movements).
Step 5: Download the generated clip, place it between your two original videos, and apply a short crossfade or smooth cut to hide the seams.

This method works for teleporting, outfit changes, mic tosses, and more.

Save this post so you can reference the prompt later, and tag a creator who needs to try this! 🎬

#videoediting #contentcreator #editingtips #AI #genAI

items.title: The Next Evolution of AI (Qwen, MIT, Tencent)
items.summary:
Three independent ArXiv pre-prints have converged on the same scientific hypothesis: the limiting factor of frontier AI is no longer inference quality, context length, or even reasoning ability. 

Instead, the next generation of intelligent systems may be defined by their capacity for recursive cognitive organization: the autonomous formation of evidence graphs, the maintenance of coherent long-horizon behavioral trajectories, and ultimately the evolution of their own representational geometry. See also RSI.

My video synthesizes these seemingly unrelated works into a unified theory of AI's next paradigm, arguing that we are witnessing a transition from intelligence as statistical prediction to intelligence as the dynamic self-organization of cognition itself.

The next evolution of AI is not a model that produces better answers inside a fixed problem. It is a system that constructs its evidence, preserves its purpose across time, and reorganizes its own conceptual space when the problem demands it.

items.title: Reconstructing Pelé’s lost goal
items.summary:
On August 2, 1959, Pelé scored the most beautiful goal of his career: three consecutive “sombreros” without the ball touching the ground. Yet, the legendary ‘Gol da Rua Javari’ was never caught on film. We worked alongside historians, sports journalists, football legends, and Pelé’s family to reconstruct this lost moment and share it with the world.

This project was created in full partnership with the Pelé Brand, the official managers of the Pelé estate.

Rooted in education and cultural preservation, the project heads to the Pelé Museum this year. To achieve this, teams from Google DeepMind used models like Gemini Omni and Veo to transform historical fragments into moving imagery, filmed on the original pitch with authentic uniforms and a vintage ball.

By making the memory of this goal more accessible, it stands as a tribute to inspire a new generation of fans during the first World Cup without him.

The goal is on display at the Museu Pelé in Santos, Brazil.

Learn more at https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-deepmind/pele-lost-goal-reconstructed

___

No dia 2 de agosto de 1959, Pelé marcou o gol mais bonito da sua carreira: três chapéus consecutivos, sem deixar a bola tocar no chão. No entanto, o famoso “Gol da Rua Javari” nunca foi filmado. Em um trabalho em conjunto com historiadores, jornalistas esportivos, lendas do futebol e familiares do Pelé, reconstruímos esse momento antológico do futebol para o mundo todo ver.

Esse projeto foi criado em parceria com a marca Pelé, administradores oficiais do espólio do Rei Pelé.

Com foco em educação e preservação cultural, o projeto segue para o Museu Pelé este ano. Para conseguir isso, equipes do Google DeepMind usaram modelos de IA como Gemini Omni e Veo, para transformar fragmentos históricos em filmes, usando filmagens no campo original com uniformes e bola da época.

Tornar a memória desse gol acessível, é uma forma de homenagem, para inspirar as novas gerações de fãs de futebol, na primeira Copa do Mundo sem o Rei Pelé.

O “Gol da Rua Javari” está em exibição no Museu Pelé, em Santos.

items.title: AI Agents in Action
items.summary:
Book Launch with Micheal Lanham!! 

With the latest edition of AI Agents in Action you are not just understanding what AI Agents are, but designing, implementing, evaluating, and deploying them.

In this session, we’ll ask these questions:
1. People build an impressive agent demo, but struggle to make it reliable. What is the biggest gap between a working prototype and a production-ready AI agent?

2. When people say “AI agent,” they often mean very different things. How do you define an agent in the book, and what should developers stop calling an agent?

3. Many developers get stuck after basic prompting. What core components should they understand before trying to build serious agentic systems?

4. Tool use is one of the most exciting parts of agents, but also one of the riskiest. How does Model Context Protocol change the way agents connect to tools, data, and external systems?

5. Multi-agent systems sound powerful, but they can also become chaotic. When should someone use multiple agents instead of one well-designed agent?

6. Planning and reasoning are where agents often look smart until they fail unexpectedly. What are the most common reasoning failures you see, and how can builders design around them?

7. Memory and RAG are often treated as add-ons. In a useful agent, how should memory, knowledge retrieval, and context management actually work together?

8. Evaluation is a major community pain point because agent behavior is hard to test. What should teams measure to know whether an agent is improving or becoming more dangerous?

9. Deployment is where many agent projects stall. What changes when you move from running an agent locally to deploying an agentic system that users or businesses depend on?

10. If someone has read blog posts, watched demos, and tried frameworks but still feels unsure how to build agents properly, how does AI Agents in Action, Second Edition help them move from scattered knowledge to a complete mental model?

This is a live, interactive session, bring your questions for Micheal.
 
We will also giveaway Ebooks to 2 lucky winners during the session. Comment #AI to enter the raffle!
